chunk_findings.detail: `safe_filename` runs `out.strip(strip)` before `out[:max]`, but its own contract sentence says the string is "cut to ``max``, stripped of ``strip`` at both ends" (cut first), and both sibling helpers in the same module truncate *before* stripping (`slug`: `s[:limit].strip("-") or default`; `ascii_slug`: `re.sub(...)[:limit]` then `.strip("-")`). Concretely, with the documented call shape `safe_filename(s, max=80, strip="-")` and `s = "a" + "-b"*40` (81 chars), the strip step is a no-op (leading `a`, trailing `b`), the cut at 80 lands on the `-` at index 79, and the function returns an 80-character name ending in `-`. Under the order stated in the docstring (and used by every other helper here) the same input yields the 79-character name ending in `b`. So any caller in the rest of this change that passes a length cap together with `strip` gets names with a trailing separator that the helpers being replaced did not produce; the trailing sentence "The order is replace, strip, cut: callers that cut first say so in ``max``'s place" contradicts the primary description rather than resolving it.

chunk_findings.detail: The old expression built the shard name from `self.agent_id` with no length limit, preserving every character (`"".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in self.agent_id)`). The replacement calls `safe_filename(self.agent_id, repl="_", unicode=True)`, and per this change's own intent `safe_filename` has a default `max=80`, so the result is now truncated to 80 characters. Any agent id longer than 80 characters therefore maps to a different file name than before, which orphans the previously written shard (existing `.jsonl` history becomes unreachable), and worse, two distinct long agent ids that share their first 80 safe characters now collapse onto the same path. For example `agent_id = "x"*100 + "-a"` and `agent_id = "x"*100 + "-b"` both produce the same truncated safe name and thus the same `shard` path, so two agents would append to one log file. The old code could not collide for these inputs. Passing an explicit larger/absent max (or not truncating here) is needed to preserve the previous one-to-one mapping.

chunk_findings.detail: The change describes the merged helper as `safe_filename(s, max=80)`, i.e. a default cap of 80 characters. But the reference expressions on lines 47 and 49 pass no `max` and expect the *untruncated* result. `SAMPLES` (line 30) contains `"x" * 120 + "-" + "y" * 10`, a 131-character input. With the documented default, `S.safe_filename(s, repl="_")` and `S.safe_filename(s, repl="_", unicode=True)` can return at most 80 characters, while `re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", s)` (and the `uni` expression on line 48) yield all 131 characters, so both assertions fail on that sample. Conversely, if the references are the "expression kept verbatim" from the code that was replaced, then the merge into a helper that defaults to `max=80` is not behaviour preserving: names longer than 80 characters that the old helpers returned intact are now silently truncated (so two distinct long inputs can collapse to the same 80-char prefix). Either the references need the `[:80]` cap (line 47/49) or the default cap cannot be 80 — as written, the test cannot pass for the 131-char sample.

chunk_findings.detail: `safe_filename` strips *before* it cuts, so truncation can re‑introduce a character that `strip` was supposed to remove, and the returned value is no longer stripped at both ends. The docstring's own contract is "replaced by ``repl`` …, then cut to ``max``, stripped of ``strip`` at both ends", and the sibling `slug()` (which does `s[:limit].strip("-")`, i.e. cut then strip) behaves the other way. Concretely, `safe_filename("aaaa-bbb", max=5, strip="-")` produces `"aaaa-bbb"` → strip to `"aaaa-bbb"` → cut to `"aaaa-"` and returns `"aaaa-"`, whereas the documented order (and `slug`) would give `"aaaa"`. Any caller that combines a length cap with a separator strip — e.g. the `safe_filename(s, max=80, strip="-")` shape the intent advertises — silently receives a name ending in the separator, so the "stripped at both ends" guarantee does not hold whenever `max` is also set.

chunk_findings.detail:
The old implementation mapped `agent_id` character-by-character with no length limit:
`"".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in self.agent_id)`.
The new call `safe_filename(self.agent_id, repl="_", unicode=True)` uses the stated default `max=80`, so it silently truncates the name. For any `agent_id` longer than 80 characters, `self.shard` now resolves to `<first-80-chars>.jsonl` instead of `<full-agent-id>.jsonl`. That changes the on-disk identity of a shard: logs previously written under the full id are no longer the target of `shard`, and `shards()` (which globs the directory) will now observe both the old full-length file and the new truncated file, or two distinct long ids that share an 80-char prefix will collide onto the same `.jsonl` and interleave records. The old code had no truncation, so this is a behavior change that was not called out in the intent; if truncation is desired it should be explicit (`max=...`) and reconciled with existing shard files.

chunk_findings.detail: `safe_filename(w.agent, repl="_", unicode=True)` is called without `max`, so it applies `safe_filename`'s default cap (`max=80`, per the stated `safe_filename(s, max=80)` signature). The code it replaces had **no** length limit: `"".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in w.agent)`. The path is then `str(d / f"{safe}-{w.pid}-{clock.run_stamp()}.json")`. Because `w.pid` is constant for a process and `clock.run_stamp()` is constant for a run (that is what "run stamp" means — the per-call timestamp is stored separately in `w.since`), the filename's only agent-dependent part is now capped at 80 chars. Concretely: a single ddflow run registers waits for two different agents whose sanitized names share their first 80 characters (e.g. two long agent labels differing only in a suffix beyond column 80). Both calls now compute the identical `safe`, hence the identical `{safe}-{pid}-{run_stamp}.json` path, and the second `_write(w)` silently overwrites the first, so one pending wait disappears. With the old untruncated join the two paths differed. `queue_path` deliberately disambiguates with a `content_digest` suffix; this path does not, so it needs an explicit large/no `max` (or a digest) here.

chunk_findings.detail: The replaced expression was `re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", check).strip("-").lower()[:30].strip("-")`, which lower-cases the result; the new call `ascii_slug(check, 30)` passes no lower-casing of its own. The sibling conversion in this same diff (`ddflow/services/importer_harness.py`, `_id_fragment`) keeps the explicit `.lower()` by calling `ascii_slug(text.lower(), limit, restrip=False)`, which shows the shared `ascii_slug` is a case-preserving ASCII replacement helper (it only substitutes non-`[A-Za-z0-9]` and trims), not a lower-casing one — otherwise the retained `.lower()` in that call would be redundant and the author's two conversions would be asymmetric. Concretely, for a pytest node id such as `check = "Test_Foo::testBar"`, the old code produced slug `test-foo-testbar`, while the new call produces `Test-Foo-testBar` (before the 30-char cap). Because this slug is fed into `IDS.render(cfg, "ci_bug", slug=slug, digest=digest)`, every check with an uppercase character now renders a different `ci_bug` id than before, so previously recorded bug entries for the same check are no longer matched by their slug prefix — the exact deduplication this function exists to provide ("that share a prefix ... from being one bug"). The fix is to preserve the original transformation, e.g. `ascii_slug(check.lower(), 30)` (or have `ascii_slug` lower-case internally and drop the now-stale explicit `.lower()` in `_id_fragment` for consistency).

chunk_findings.detail: The old expression `re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", check).strip("-").lower()[:30].strip("-")` folded the check to lower case; the replacement `ascii_slug(check, 30)` no longer does. The sibling call site added in this same change, `ddflow/services/importer_harness.py::_id_fragment`, deliberately lower-cases its input (`ascii_slug(text.lower(), limit, restrip=False)`) precisely because `ascii_slug` keeps the input's case (it is an ASCII *character* mapping, unlike `slug()` which lower-cases, and unlike `github_anchor` which lower-cases). So for a check such as `"TestFoo::Bar"` the old code produced `testfoo-bar` and the new code produces `TestFoo-Bar`, which is then baked into the id via `IDS.render(cfg, "ci_bug", slug=slug, digest=digest)`. That silently changes the generated `ci_bug` id strings (case-sensitive references/dedup keys written by earlier runs no longer match), while a `ci.py` caller that omits the lower-casing gives the opposite result from the `_id_fragment` caller of the very same helper. Either the two `ascii_slug` call sites should agree (drop `.lower()` in `_id_fragment`) or `ci.py` must restore the case folding by passing `check.lower()`.

chunk_findings.detail:
`safe_filename` trims the `strip` characters from both ends (its contract is "replaced by ``repl`` …, then cut to ``max``, stripped of ``strip`` at both ends", and the sibling `slug()` does `s[:limit].strip("-")`), but the code it replaces never stripped:

```python
safe = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in f"{agent}-q-{item}")
return _dir(repo) / f"{safe[:80]}-{digest}.json"
```

For `queue_id(repo, "claude", "x-")` the old code keeps the trailing dash — `"claude-q-x-"[:80]` → file `claude-q-x--<digest>.json` — while the new `safe_filename("claude-q-x-", repl="_", unicode=True, max=80)` strips it to `"claude-q-x"` → `claude-q-x-<digest>.json`. Because the `digest` is computed from the raw pair, both names are deterministic, so the rename is silent: queue entries written under the old name become unreachable after the upgrade (lookups/`wait`s land on a path that does not exist). The same shift applies whenever an `agent`/`item` ends in `-`, `_`, or `.`, and the 80-char cut can itself end on such a character, shaving a char off the prefix. This is a semantic change introduced by the migration and is not addressed by the earlier triage (which only discussed `max`). If stripping is not wanted here, the call sites must pass `strip=""`.

chunk_findings.detail: Same root cause, but here it also flips the `if safe != raw:` decision. For `raw = "abc-"`, every character is in the old allow set `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, so the old expression `re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "", raw)[:48]` yields `"abc-"` which equals `raw`, and the un-hashed session id is used. The new `safe_filename(raw, repl="", max=48)` strips the trailing dash to `"abc"`, which no longer equals `raw`, so the function now takes the hashing/disambiguation branch for an input that previously required no mangling. The same raw harness session id therefore maps to a different ddflow session id than before, which breaks continuity for any already-persisted session keyed by it. (Also reachable when the 48-char cut lands on a stripped character.)

chunk_findings.detail:
The hunk deletes `diff_stat`'s only untracked-file accounting —

```python
-    u = W.git(cwd, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", ".", *FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDE)
-    if u.ok and u.out.strip():
-        out["untracked"] = len(u.out.splitlines())
```

— and adds nothing in its place. Before this change, calling `diff_stat(cwd)` in a repo with, say, two untracked files returned a dict containing `"untracked": 2`; after it, the key is simply absent (the function falls straight through to `return out`). That is a silent behavior regression for any consumer that reads `out["untracked"]` (KeyError) or uses `.get("untracked", 0)` and now always sees 0.

It also contradicts the docstring introduced in this very diff: `_untracked_paths` says *"callers that cannot tell the two apart; the fingerprint and `diff_stat` can, and do"*, i.e. `diff_stat` is supposed to distinguish "git could not list untracked files" (None) from "no untracked files" ([]). The correct conversion of the deleted block would have been to call `_untracked_listing(cwd)` here and set `out["untracked"] = UNLISTED` (or equivalent) when it returns `None` — instead the block was removed outright, so `diff_stat` no longer calls any untracked listing at all and cannot "do" what the docstring claims. The input that demonstrates it: any worktree with untracked files, or any git failure during listing, produces a `diff_stat` result with no `untracked` field, where the old code produced one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/evidence.py (diff_stat, removal at old lines 139-153)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own description of the API it introduces is "git.paths, git.status (parsed porcelain -z) and git.unmerged", and the two other call sites in this diff use exactly the names from that description (`GIT.unmerged` in `ports.py` and `promotions.py`). The listing site, however, was rewritten from `W.git_paths(root, "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard")` to `GIT.files(root, "all")` — a helper name that this change never introduces. If `infra/git.py` exposes the listing helper as `GIT.paths` (the name the change advertises, and the natural rename of the old `git_paths`), then `propose()` raises `AttributeError: module 'ddflow.infra.git' has no attribute 'files'` for every repository, so `precommit.propose(root)` crashes instead of returning a `Proposal` (or `None`), and hook proposal is entirely broken. Even in the best case where some other module defines `files`, the listing site is calling a function with different semantics than the `git.paths` helper the other sites and the description assume, which needs to be reconciled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/precommit.py:164 (`propose`)

chunk_findings.detail: The three listing call sites were changed to `GIT.files(tree, "untracked")` / `GIT.files(tree, "all")`, but the new helper exposed by `infra.git` is named `git.paths` — the stated intent says "git.paths, git.status (parsed porcelain -z) and git.unmerged; the listing, porcelain and unmerged sites use them", i.e. the listing sites are supposed to call `git.paths`. `GIT` is bound by `from ..infra import git as GIT`, so the import itself succeeds, but `git` has no `files` attribute. The failure is therefore deferred to call time: any invocation of `_changed` (line 113, when building the changed-path set), `_listed` (line 166, the listing helper) or `_churn` (line 459, the untracked churn loop) raises `AttributeError: module 'ddflow.infra.git' has no attribute 'files'`. Concretely, calling `_listed(tree)` on any worktree now crashes instead of returning the tracked+untracked path list, so the listing/selection path that this change is supposed to migrate is broken. The correct calls should go through the `GIT.paths` helper introduced by this change.

chunk_findings.detail: This hunk deletes the only code that produced the `untracked` field of `diff_stat` (`u = W.git(...)`, `if u.ok and u.out.strip(): out["untracked"] = len(u.out.splitlines())`) and adds no replacement in its place — the deletion sits immediately before `return out`, so `diff_stat` now never emits `"untracked"` at all. The new docstring of `_untracked_paths` asserts that "the fingerprint and `diff_stat` can, and do" tell a failed listing (`None`) apart from an empty one, but `diff_stat` no longer calls `_untracked_listing`/`GIT.files`/`_untracked_paths`, so it cannot distinguish anything and the claim is false. The stated intent was that the listing site should *use* the new `git`/`STATE_EXCLUDE` helpers, not that it should be removed. Concretely, for a repo containing an untracked file, the pre-change `diff_stat(cwd)` returned e.g. `{..., "untracked": 1}`, whereas now it returns `{...}` with no key; a consumer doing `diff_stat(...)["untracked"]` raises `KeyError`, and one doing `diff_stat(...).get("untracked", 0)` silently sees `0`, so any untracked-files gate/evidence check stops firing without any error.

chunk_findings.detail: The listing site does not call the helper this change introduces. The intent enumerates the new git module's API as `git.paths`, `git.status` and `git.unmerged`, and says "the listing, porcelain and unmerged sites use them" — the listing site here is exactly the file listing that previously went through `W.git_paths(root, "ls-files", ...)`, so the replacement should be `GIT.paths(root, "all")`. `GIT.files` is not one of the names introduced (the module is imported as `GIT` from `..infra.git`), so any call to `propose()` — e.g. running the pre-commit hook proposal for any repository — evaluates the attribute `GIT.files`, which does not exist, and raises `AttributeError` before `detect_stacks` ever runs. Hook proposal is therefore broken outright, not merely degraded (the accompanying `paths is None` guard is never reached). If instead `GIT.files` really exists in `infra/git.py`, then the intent's claim that the listing site uses `git.paths` is false and the two must be reconciled; either way this call site and the declared API disagree.
